title: Hawaii lieutenant governor indicted on bribery charges tied to COVID testing contract
dek: Democratic Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke faces federal indictment on charges of conspiracy to commit bribery, bribery, and falsifying campaign reports, allegedly related to a $35,000 bribe from a businessman connected to a state COVID-19 testing contract. Hawaii Gov. Josh Green called for her resignation hours after the indictment was announced.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Luke allegedly accepted two $5,000 checks in January 2022 from businessman Tobi Solidum, who promised a total of $70,000, according to prosecutors; Luke admitted taking the initial checks but denied taking additional money or allowing it to influence her legislative decisions.
bottom_line: Luke faces trial on charges that will require prosecutors to prove the alleged payments influenced official action tied to the COVID-19 testing contracts. How quickly she responds to the governor's call for resignation, and whether additional defendants cooperate with prosecutors, will shape the investigation's trajectory.
body: Hawaii's Democratic Lieutenant Governor Sylvia Luke has been indicted on charges of criminal conspiracy to commit bribery, bribery, and falsifying candidate committee reports, according to reporting by Fox News. The charges stem from alleged conduct dating to 2022, when she served as a state lawmaker.

The indictment alleges that Luke accepted $10,000 in two installments from local businessman and lobbyist Tobi Solidum, who promised an additional $60,000, for a total commitment of $70,000. According to the indictment, Solidum met with Luke at a steakhouse in January 2022 and gave her two checks of $5,000 each, made out to her campaign committee, Friends of Sylvia Luke. Solidum allegedly told Luke "By next week, we'll have 35, so it will be halfway to our 70," per prosecutors' account in the indictment documents. Luke's alleged reply was "Oh wow" and "That's terrific."

Solidum represented the National Kidney Foundation of Hawaii, which held contracts with the state to provide COVID-19 testing sites. Prosecutors allege that Solidum was attempting to leverage his relationship with Luke as she prepared to run for lieutenant governor, saying to another state representative, "All I gotta do is give her more money now," according to the indictment.

The indictment also names four other defendants swept up in what Fox News reports was an investigation by Hawaii Attorney General Anne Lopez that originated as an offshoot of a federal bribery probe. Those charged include businessman Tobi Solidum, former state representative Ryan Yamane, Hawaii Transportation Department official Ford Fuchigami, and Leo Asunción, a former official for Hawaii's public utilities commission.

Luke has acknowledged accepting the two $5,000 checks but denied taking additional payments. In a social media post, she stated, "I never granted special favors to a contributor," and said she "prized integrity and honesty above all throughout her career." She denied that any money influenced her lawmaking.

Hours after the indictment was announced, Hawaii Gov. Josh Green publicly called for Luke to step down. Green told local outlet Maui Now on Friday: "The lieutenant governor needs to consider formally resigning to address this matter and so that the state of Hawai'i can move forward."
